goldens.comment: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.
goldens.reasoning: C1 points out the same misuse of the Error log level for non-error output and suggests Debug/Info instead.

goldens.comment: The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.
goldens.reasoning: C2 flags the same ticker change from 10 minutes to 1 minute and the extra DB load it causes.

candidates: Cleanup batches log at Error level on the success path and include the full list of IDs, which can flood logs and potentially expose internal record IDs - should use Debug/Info level and avoid logging the IDs, reserving Error for actual failures

Cleanup service ticker was reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which will increase DB/file cleanup load and can cause the cleanup loop to run almost continuously if a cycle takes >1m - this change appears unrelated to the MySQL deadlock fix and should be restored to previous cadence

Building the SQLite inline ID list with repeated fmt.Sprintf in a loop is O(n²) in allocations and can become expensive for large batches - should use strings.Builder with strconv.FormatInt to build the IN list efficiently

Test case inserts ~40k annotations and uses a 32k batch size, which can make CI slow/flaky without adding much coverage beyond exercising the batch size > SQLite parameter limit path - should reduce dataset while still exceeding 999 parameters (e.g., ~3003 annotations with batch size 1000) and update the test name which incorrectly mentions a specific SQLite version
